title: Lift a steeped infuser out of a glass teapot by its thin handle bar, shake off the drips over the pot, set it on a saucer and put the lid back
instruction: Take the steeped infuser out of the teapot: lid off, basket out by its handle bar, shaken up and down three times over the pot to shed the drips, set on the saucer, then the lid back on the pot.
context: Making loose-leaf tea in a glass teapot is an everyday routine (over 159 million Americans drink tea on a given day: Tea Association of the USA, via the US Census Bureau, census.gov/newsroom/stories/hot-tea-month.html), and ending the steep means getting the damp infuser out and keeping its drips off the table. What is distinctive is the physical core: the only handle is a 2.4 mm flat bar whose top sits 4 mm below the rim, the basket clears the 9.6 cm mouth by under 4 mm a side, the lifted basket hangs from a thin pinch and has to be shaken three times over the pot without losing its leaves, and the lid is then set down and re-seated by its 27 mm knob.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the table top. Teapot: clear borosilicate glass, round belly 15 cm across, 15 cm tall to the rim, mouth 9.6 cm across (inside), spout and handle out to 24.2 cm overall, 0.40 kg empty, holding 500 g of room-temperature water (the usual steeping level; it is the pot's ballast, and the pot must not be disturbed), standing on its foot at (36.0, 0.0) with its handle towards the robot's left and its spout to the right. Lid: clear glass, 10.5 cm across with a 2.7 cm round knob, 0.08 kg, 18.0 cm above the table at the knob, resting on the rim. Infuser: stainless steel mesh basket 8.8 cm across at its rim and 13 cm deep with a 2.4 mm thick flat handle bar across its top (8.7 cm long, 1.1 cm tall, its top 4 mm below the pot's rim), 0.139 kg, standing on the pot's floor with the bar running forward-back (x). In it: about 23 g of damp steeped black tea leaves (8 g of dry leaf, steeped 3 minutes), lying in the bottom 2 cm; the damp leaves and the wet basket are what drip when it is lifted. Saucer: clear glass, 14.2 cm across and 1.4 cm tall, at (30.0, 23.0). A ring marked on the table round the pot's foot (4 cm radius) shows the pot's shift. Rig protection for real trials: a 60 x 40 cm waterproof drip mat under the pot and the saucer.
scoring: Tools: phone video from the side (60 frames per second, a 2 cm marker in view) and from above, a ruler, a kitchen scale. Scored on the final state, after both grippers are clear; the same rule is computed from the bodies' poses in simulation. 0 for the whole run if the pot is shifted more than 4 cm (its foot leaves the marked ring) or tipped more than 15 degrees at any time. Otherwise: 0.25 with the basket out of the pot and resting clear of its mouth (its axis more than 7.5 cm from the pot's); 0.5 with it resting on the saucer (its axis within 3 cm of the saucer's centre, tilted less than 15 degrees); 0.75 with, in addition, leaves outside the basket weighing under 2 g (at least 90 % of the leaves still in it) and the basket having been shaken over the pot: three down-up strokes of at least 2 cm each, the third ending within 2 seconds of the first, all with its underside at least 1 cm above the pot's rim, its axis within 4 cm of the pot's and tilted less than 25 degrees; 1.0 with, in addition, the lid back on the pot (its centre within 6 mm of the pot's axis, resting on the rim within 4 mm of the seated height and tilted less than 5 degrees). Reported with each real trial, but not part of the score: the water on the saucer after the carry (the weight gain of a folded paper towel on it, in grams) and the same trial with a still 3-second hold in place of the shake, as a control.
reset_notes: Put the pot back on its marked ring with the lid on and 500 g of room-temperature water in it. Tip the old leaves out of the basket, put in 8 g of fresh dry black tea, steep the basket in the pot for 3 minutes (water at 40 C or cooler for trials on the robot), then leave it standing in the pot with its bar running forward-back and put the lid on. Wipe the saucer, the drip mat and the robot's fingertips dry and lay a fresh folded paper towel on the saucer. A new trial can start as soon as the pot is back on its ring (about 5 minutes with the steep).
fidelity: Teapot, lid, basket and saucer are rigid bodies (NVIDIA USDCraft-10K models split into parts; colliders are boxes and convex hulls); the basket's mesh walls are solid. The damp leaves are 200 rigid pieces (r 2.5-3.5 mm, 23 g) with no stickiness. Water is not simulated (the pot's 500 g is added to its mass); dripping is represented by a rule: three quick strokes of the basket over the pot, which in a real trial is what sheds the drips.
scores: demo: 1.0 (all steps incl. three shake strokes, scores 1.0 at 51.4 s / 1,028 steps); Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,000 steps; both arms moved to a hover position in front of the pot within the first 15 seconds and stayed there for the rest of the run, so the lid and the basket never moved)
